title: Homepage
lead: Pick an analysis, search one or more genes, choose a tissue and data version, then open the gene network.

pairs.caption: Typing IL1B in the gene search
IL1B and TNF chosen, ready to show the network

differences.existing: Gene search gives no suggestions until an analysis is chosen. Typing IL1B with no analysis showed 0 results.
differences.proposed: Suggestions appear right away. Choosing a gene switches the analysis to Networks.
differences.evidence: Live: humanbase.io screen reader text '0 results available for search term IL1B'; proposed HomeSearch.tsx note text

differences.existing: Flat list of 10 tools, each with a one-line description.
differences.proposed: Same tools grouped under Network analysis, Variant effects, Sequences and Browsers, with a 'Compare them' link.
differences.evidence: Both menus opened on the live sites; HomeSearch.tsx footer links to /sequence-tools/

differences.existing: Typing 'cancer' lists genes with tags showing the matched disease (for example ING1: head and neck cancer, cancer). TNF suggestions also show pathway tags.
differences.proposed: Typing 'cancer' lists the same genes but with no tags. Pressing Enter treats 'cancer' as a gene and reports 'Not found'.

differences.existing: IL1B, BRCA1, PTEN, cancer, autism, plus three gene sets. With Networks chosen, the list drops to IL1B, BRCA1, PTEN, cancer, autism.
differences.proposed: IL1B, BRCA1, PTEN and 'Autism gene set'. No 'cancer' or 'autism' term examples. Renal and synapse sets live in Modules mode.

differences.existing: Clicking IL1B chooses Networks and adds IL1B to the gene table.
differences.proposed: Clicking IL1B chooses Networks and adds IL1B to the gene table.
differences.evidence: Live: both sites, URL stays on the homepage

differences.existing: Typing 'IL1B TNF' turns the field into a text box; Enter lists both genes under 'Search Results'.
differences.proposed: Typing 'IL1B TNF' and Enter matches both. Pasted lists split on new lines, commas, semicolons and tabs.

differences.existing: 'Selected Genes': Search term, Entrez id, Standard name, Aliases, Description, remove button.
differences.proposed: 'How your genes matched': You typed, Gene with name, Entrez ID, Status, remove button, and counts of matched, to check and not found. No aliases column.
Each term gets a status: Matched, To check (choose between candidates) or Not found.
differences.evidence: Proposed showed 'cancer: Not found'. Ask what the existing site does with a symbol it cannot match or that matches several genes.

differences.area: Gene missing from a data version
differences.proposed: Warns when a gene is not in GIANT or MAGE and offers to remove it or switch version.

differences.existing: 'Select network' list with a filter box; 'global' is an option.
differences.proposed: 'Tissue' list with a filter box; leave empty for the global network. Changing data version clears the tissue.

differences.existing: GIANT by default; options GIANT and MAGE.
differences.proposed: GIANT by default; options GIANT and MAGE.

differences.existing: /gene/3553+7124. Tissue and data version are not in the address.
differences.proposed: /networks/?entrez=3553&entrez=7124&version=v1, with &tissue= when a tissue is chosen.
differences.evidence: Live result URLs after submitting IL1B + TNF

differences.existing: Links to /gene/3553 and opens the global network.
differences.evidence: Live: clicked on humanbase.io, tissue showed 'global'; home/content.ts

differences.existing: Analyses, Resources, Documentation, About, Mailing list.
differences.proposed: Network analysis, Sequence analysis, Data, Docs, About, Jobs.
A 'What's new' list on the homepage with an 'All updates' link.

differences.existing: 'Mailing list' in the top bar and a floating 'Contact us' button.
differences.proposed: 'Release notes by email, Subscribe' and 'Contact us' in the footer.

differences.existing: 'data-driven predictions of gene expression, function, regulation, and interactions in human'.
differences.proposed: 'Predictions of gene function, regulation and interactions in human', plus a line citing 7,463 genome-scale datasets.
differences.evidence: HomePage.tsx leads. Ask whether 7,463 is the right dataset count and whether 'expression' should stay in the title.
